installedBy: root integrator (example values; run `node scripts/release/project-routing.mjs init` to write a real record)

enforcement._comment: warn: a `contribute` call without --project/--lane is accepted and stamped routing.mode=legacy with a visible warning. refuse: such a call fails. Root flips this to refuse at cutover; ATOMIC_ACRES_ROUTING_REQUIRED=1 in the environment has the same effect without a registry.

integration.destination: pull request into main; contributors never push main
integration._comment: expectedSha is the origin/main this record was written against. The guard refuses when fetched origin/main differs: re-run init/readback after every integration rather than trusting a stale record.

inspectedPreview._comment: Which exact SHA a human last inspected and what they said. This field is a record, never an approval; the guard never writes it.

production.verification: fetched gh-pages manifest only; no cache-busted live smoke recorded
production._comment: The publisher is python scripts/orchestration/publish_pass<N>.py from the canonical checkout. This record describes production; it never publishes.

rollback._comment: The pinned safe backup (HF-400). --rollback re-points the default without deleting a tree.

protectedCheckouts.reason: Owner's designated Pass 62 netcode benchmark checkout; must stay byte-exact. Refused as a contribution worktree even if a lane names it.

closure._comment: integrated: laneHeadSha must be an ancestor of integratedIntoSha, which must be an ancestor of the integration ref. Retirement of the worktree is a separate manual step after `lane-close` passes; the guard removes nothing.

closure.reason: Owner rejected the visual result; unique commits preserved for later reference.
closure._comment: rejected: at least one preservation proof is required and is verified (ref resolves to laneHeadSha, or bundle verifies and lists laneHeadSha). A dirty worktree is never closable.
